newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Eni to merge with unit Agip.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Eni to merge with unit Agip.

text.p: Italy's state-controlled energy group Eni said it intended to absorb its oil exploration and production unit Agip.
Eni said the merger, which must be approved by a shareholders' meeting planned for June 19 or 20, was intended to increase efficiency in the group's operations.
Eni is the sole shareholder in Agip.

Eni said its board also intended to ask the extraordinary shareholders' meeting to be allowed for a period of five years to issue bonds which could be convertible into shares in its subsidiaries for a total of up to 5.0 trillion lire.
"The proposal allows us to be able to make timely use of opportunities offered by the financial markets," it said.
It also announced it intended to pay a 1996 dividend of 240 lire per share, compared with 215 lire in 1995.
